site.name: Dzmitryi Kharlanau — SAP Learning & AMS Optimization

objective.primary: Make two site jobs unambiguous to search systems and AI agents: SAP learning/interview/assessment practice for professionals, and SAP AMS optimization for teams reducing recurring operational work. Route MDG, integration, logistics and practical AI as supporting domains inside those jobs rather than as competing top-level promises.
targetQuestions: Where should an SAP professional go to practise interviews, assessments and decision-making?
Which reviewed and indexable learning surfaces can currently support SAP interview and assessment queries?
Where should an SAP service owner go to reduce repeat incidents, manual recovery and unreliable operational work?
What SAP AMS diagnostic, integration reliability and master-data stability services are available?
Which supporting MDG, integration, logistics and AI evidence surfaces belong to each primary direction?
Which learning and service routes are still noindex or review-gated and must not be presented as verified search entry points?
Which machine-readable interfaces, datasets, Agent Skills and MCP servers expose the site's public knowledge?
What crawler, reuse, evidence and correction policies apply to the site's public material?

entityHome.notes: The homepage exposes exactly two primary choices: Learn and Improve AMS.

siteProfile.notes: ARWP site profile declares the two-focus routing extension and points to /ai/focus-map.json.

llmsCanonical.notes: The manifest states the two primary routes before the deeper knowledge model.

answerPages.description: Classify requests with the two-focus map first. For search-grounded learning queries, use the reviewed/indexable Interview Readiness hub and reviewed Decision Cards. The /learn/, /labs/assessment/ and broad /labs/enterprise-context/ routes remain useful practice/navigation surfaces but are noindex. For AMS queries, use the AMS service pillar plus reviewed diagnostic and evidence pages, while preserving the publication state of supporting service drafts.

originalResearch.description: Publish bounded experiments, datasets and field-derived analyses as supporting evidence for the two primary directions, with explicit review state and limitations instead of creating additional top-level site promises.

protocolObservatory.description: Add a dated source-backed observatory only if agentic-web protocol tracking becomes a recurring subject of this professional site rather than duplicating the dedicated ARWP project.

comparisonPages.description: Add explicit comparison pages only where recurring SAP learning or AMS decisions benefit from stable side-by-side trade-offs and evidence.

conceptDefinitions.description: Use the reviewed Atlas glossary and canonical entity pages for stable supporting definitions after the primary learning-versus-AMS route is chosen.

claimsRegistry.description: Introduce stable claim identifiers only for high-value professional or technical assertions that need explicit evidence, review date and supersession history.

evidenceReceipts.description: Add replayable evidence receipts for selected generated or evaluated artifacts when exact input, output and provenance materially improve trust.

crawlerMatrix.description: Publish a dated machine-readable view of the site's explicit robots policy, separating search and user-directed retrieval from model-training crawler access.

agentFetchLab.description: Measure whether real agents correctly distinguish learning requests from live AMS-improvement requests before adding more special-purpose discovery files.

knowledgeGraph.description: Maintain a canonical JSON-LD graph connecting person identity, the website and the site's public machine-readable discovery and trust surfaces.

citationVisuals.description: Publish a bounded set of reusable learning diagrams and AMS diagnostic visuals with stable URLs, source notes and explicit reuse terms where visuals materially improve comprehension.

openReuseAssets.description: Create a dedicated media and reuse-rights surface only when reusable public diagrams, learning assets or research artifacts warrant a separate permission model.

trustCenter.description: Publish one canonical trust surface covering identity, review model, citation, security reporting, crawler policy, corrections and evidence boundaries for both primary directions.

correctionsLedger.description: Maintain a public machine-readable ledger for material corrections instead of silently changing important published factual claims.

softwareProvenance.description: The website is not represented as a released software package; repository history and CI provide source history, but no package-level provenance or security attestation is claimed.

persistentIdentifiers.description: Use DOI or another externally issued persistent identifier only for datasets or research artifacts where durable citation value justifies it, and never claim one before issuance.

externalTrustSignals.description: Expose independent trust signals only when an external source actually exists and its scope can be stated without turning it into a correctness or expertise certificate.

externalDistribution.description: Distribute selected substantial learning or AMS knowledge externally while preserving this site as the canonical source of record.

aiVisibility.description: Measure the two primary directions separately: learning/interview/assessment discovery versus commercial AMS-optimization discovery. Keep query clusters, landing pages and downstream actions separate so broad SAP traffic cannot hide weak intent fit.

localization.description: Keep English as the canonical machine semantics and add reviewed language routing only when localized public content can preserve the same two-focus intent model reliably.

history.description: Expose a concise machine-readable site evolution timeline if product and knowledge-surface maturity becomes useful context for readers and agents.

vocabulary.definition: The site has two primary audience jobs: SAP learning/interview/assessment practice for an individual, and SAP AMS optimization for a live team or service problem. Integration, MDG, logistics and practical AI are supporting domains inside those routes.

After a primary route is selected, the preferred knowledge chain establishes the enterprise domain, selects a reviewed decision, inspects an applied scenario and follows the claim back to reviewed evidence.

A site publication state indicating that content has passed the site's review and indexing rules and is allowed into public retrieval surfaces; structural completeness or inclusion in a navigation hub alone does not imply this state.

signals.name: two-focus search visibility
signals.description: Track impressions, queries and landing-page performance separately for SAP learning/assessment intent and SAP AMS-optimization intent without claiming causal ranking gains.

signals.name: AI route accuracy
signals.description: Sample observable AI citations and referrals to check whether learning requests reach learning evidence and live operational problems reach AMS evidence.

signals.name: referring domains
signals.description: Track external sources that cite or link to reviewed learning, AMS, datasets and professional evidence.

measurement.privacy: Use aggregate and privacy-minimized visibility signals; do not create visitor-level browsing histories or infer private user intent from retrieval telemetry.
